== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' was a farmer at '''Drumgreenagh, County Armagh'''. A deed of assignment dated 13 February 1786 identifies his wife as '''Jane Murphy''', daughter of the late '''Thomas Murphy'''. The deed recites that Thomas died intestate leaving a widow and five children, and that a one-fifth share of land at Lislea fell to Jane.<ref name="Deed1786">Registry of Deeds, Ireland, memorial of deed of assignment, David Murphy to John Glasgow, deed dated 13 February 1786, registered 22 December 1792; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-VDTD FamilySearch image].</ref>

For £25, David Murphy assigned John two acres, one rood and thirty-five perches at Lislea, with the associated renewal rights. The memorial was registered on 22 December 1792. William Henry and [[Glasgow-4014|Nathaniel Glasgow of Drumgreenagh]], farmer, witnessed the transaction.<ref name="Deed1786" />

John's birth is shown only as before 1768, an estimated boundary consistent with his being married and transacting land in 1786. His death occurred after the deed date; no exact death record has been identified.

== Research Notes ==
=== Drumgreenagh father hypothesis ===

The older Drumgreenagh farmer John [[Glasgow-4031]] is the preferred probable father of the later farmer John [[Glasgow-3439]], at 64% subjective confidence. The combined argument is the same full name, the same specific townland and farming occupation, and a normal two-generation chronology. The older John was already a married farmer in 1786; the younger account’s approximate 1794 birth fits a child of that household. It is a more specific family comparison than a generic same-surname Armagh or Scottish father. Prefer this direct local lineal model over leaving the later four-child household disconnected from its already identified earlier surname household. The connection is an inference from the combined evidence, not a parent clause or an implication of the connectivity score.

No source names the younger John’s father. The older man’s purchased property was at Lislea, although he resided at Drumgreenagh; no inspected title chain proves that he and the 1839 farmer occupied the same farm. The 1828 Drumgreenagh John probate-index entry is not treated as a proved death, inheritance or link between them: its document type, individual identity and surviving text remain unresolved. Nathaniel-4014 is another older local relative and possible father; an uncle, other collateral, another John, or another unrepresented father remains possible. Both 1786 adults lack recorded ages. The younger John’s 1794 birth is uncertain and has no recovered primary age source in this review, so it cannot absolutely exclude his being the 1786 man at an older age. The preferred father model keeps the two accounts separate without claiming that distinction proved or merging them. Jane Murphy is the older John’s documented wife, but is not assigned as the younger John’s mother. All vital fields, spouses, children and earlier parent grades remain unchanged. The 64% is an individual comparative judgment for this entire father-profile proposition, including the profile and generation assumptions, not a measured probability.

Verify the 1839 freeholder entry and the source of the reported 1794 birth/1849 death. Identify the type of the 1828 probate entry. Trace the Drumgreenagh and Lislea leases, rent rolls and valuation holdings for an explicit son or successor, and test Nathaniel as a separate family option.<ref name="DrumgreenaghFamily2026">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-VDTD Registry of Deeds, John Glasgow and Jane Murphy; deed 13 February 1786, registered 22 December 1792; previously inspected account reused]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/search/results?datasetname=ireland%2C%20ulster%20freeholders&firstname=john&lastname=glasgow Ireland, Ulster Freeholders: John Glasgow, farmer, Drumgreenagh, 1839; PRONI T/808/14961 vol.123 p.1 line151; held citation, original not rechecked]. Existing source accounts reconsidered 20 October 2026; original entries not newly inspected.</ref>


This John cannot be [[Glasgow-3439|John Glasgow born about 1794]], who belonged to a later Drumgreenagh generation. The shared residence makes a family relationship plausible, but the 1786 memorial names no child of John and Jane.

The memorial also states no relationship between John and Nathaniel Glasgow.
